taskRules.target: Sort notes by onset, then pitch, then ID. From index floor(n/2), take the first note whose pitch/onset address is unique and whose edited result neither collides with another note address nor leaves MIDI range 0-127. Instances sharing a window choose in instance order; a later instance skips notes already targeted.
taskRules.velocity: Transcriptions carry placeholder velocity 64, so real windows receive synthetic dynamics from r01-pilot-velocity-v1: per-work base 64-84, phrase depth 6-12 and phase 0-7 quarters; per note, beat accent +6 (+4 more on a four-quarter downbeat) within 1/16 quarter of a beat, +2 within 1/16 of an off-beat, a triangular eight-quarter phrase swell, register emphasis round((pitch - median pitch) / 6) clamped to +/-4, and jitter -5..5; rounded and clamped to 20-120. They are not recovered performance dynamics.
taskRules.shiftRange: The first of [4,6), [6,8), [8,10), [10,12) containing at least two onsets whose shifted result has no pitch/onset collision.
taskRules.editVelocity: 91, or 37 if the target velocity is already 91.
taskRules.synthetic: Seeded SHA-256 draws from r01-pilot-synthetic-v1. p02/p04 spreads are even 1/512 cells; p07 (revision 4) uses six members with odd and even cells, so halving leaves the 1/512 grid.
taskRules.sounding: Work C. T is the note onset nearest quarter 8 (earlier on a tie) at which another note ends and a third note is held across (onset < T < end); a note sounds at T when onset <= T < onset + duration.
taskRules.transposePitch: Work C. Among pitches with 5-10 notes, by descending count then ascending pitch, the first whose notes can all move up two semitones within MIDI range without landing on an existing pitch/onset address.
taskRules.shiftTransposeRange: Work A. Over distinct onsets F >= 4 in ascending order, T is the first distinct onset >= F + 2; take the first [F, T) holding 4-12 notes whose shifted (+1/8) and transposed (+2) results collide with no other address. Both bounds are note onsets.
taskRules.nearMiss: Work B. Same-pitch onset pairs x < y with y - x <= 1 quarter, by x in the edit-target order from the median and excluding the p05 target; F = floor(x) and T = y, and x must be the only note of that pitch in [F, T). The note at T lies just outside the half-open range.
taskRules.groupTiming: Package v5 (D63): p13-p16 are synthetic and seeded from r01-pilot-synthetic-v1 under new draw domains (p13-v5 to p16-v5). Timed groups have whole-quarter anchors, a positive common delay and strictly increasing 1/512 spread cells from 0; timing-free groups have no anchor, delay or spread. Note-array order equals C4 block traversal (timed groups, then notes homed in timing-free groups, then loose notes) in every input and expected state, so neither format must reorder rows or add order cells.
taskRules.readDerivedWindow: p13: three timed groups (5, 4 and 5 members), a timing-free group with two untimed notes and one timed member, and three loose notes. X is the derived onset of the first group's third member and Y that of the third group's third member, so omitting the common delay moves a note across each bound. One loose note shares a timed member's onset, so the ID tie-break applies.
taskRules.groupExisting: p14: five loose notes whose onsets equal anchor + delay + spread for a hidden decomposition (delay an odd multiple of 1/128, spreads 1/512 cells) become one timed group appended after an existing timed group; the expected spreads reproduce every onset.
taskRules.moveMember: p15: groups are ordered target, source, timing-free. The moved note is the source group's first member and also belongs to the timing-free group; its stated spread exceeds every target spread, so appending it keeps note-array order.
taskRules.retimeTwo: p16: the first group's anchor moves later by an odd multiple of 1/16 and the second group's spreads (odd cells after 0) double. A timing-free group holds one member of each and an untimed note; a loose note lies between the two groups.

stageRules.seeds: The synthetic draws use r01-pilot-synthetic-v2 and the real-source velocities r01-pilot-velocity-v2, in place of the development seeds named in taskRules.
stageRules.roles: Works 4-6 of the seeded order (or their replacements) fill roles A, B and C; taskRules' Work A/B/C refer to these roles.
stageRules.windows: Densest admissible window with target-rule refusal (r01-pilot-selection-rules-v3).

limits: Rigorous stage: versions frozen by R01-D1; works and seeds are fresh (R01-D2) and were not seen in development.
Real-source windows are transcriptions; their velocities are seeded synthetic dynamics over placeholder 64, not recovered performance dynamics or musical intent.
Source tasks exclude current-document and Producer Pal arms: no annotation adapter or sidecar is supplied (pilot draft 2, review answer 3).
Package v3 (E370): selector, spelling and contract wording revised, the TASK SCOPE block folded into the contract prose, and the bar|beat card documents d/t suffixes. Inputs and oracles equal v2.

Package v4 (D61): p01, p06, p07, p08 and p09 are harder replacements under new IDs (boundary read, multi-note transpose, off-grid halving with an anchor move, a two-step onset-bounded range, a near-miss delete); p09 and p10 share a conditional-refusal response line. Inputs equal v3; p01 now reads work C.

Package v5 (D63): adds four synthetic group-timing source tasks, p13-p16 (read a derived-onset window, group existing notes, move a member between timed groups, retime two groups). p01-p12 equal v4. Note-array order equals C4 block traversal in every new fixture.
Scoring follows D59: functionally equivalent parsed answers pass; rational strings compare by value.
Native Producer Pal parsing is tolerant; semantic pass does not establish canonical or strictly valid syntax.
Cell order is build order; trial order comes from the pilot runner plan.
Common performed scoring normalizes once at 1/512; IDs/order are not cross-format scored. Source scoring is exact.
